message.content:
Below are two ways you can launch a **Compute‑Engine** VM that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000‑equivalent GPU (the closest supported GPU family on GCP is the **Tesla A100**) running **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important:**  
> *GCP does not expose “RTX A6000” directly – the closest GPU family is `nvidia-tesla-a100`. If you specifically need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to check if your region offers the `nvidia-tesla-a6000` accelerator type (currently only available in a few zones). Replace the accelerator type below with `nvidia-tesla-a6000` if it’s available in your zone.*

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI Command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
    --zone us-central1-a \                     # <-- change to your preferred zone
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \             # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \   # <-- replace with nvidia-tesla-a6000 if available
    --boot-disk-size 50GB \                    # size of the OS disk
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \           # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \          # official Ubuntu image project
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \           # keep the same policy as EC2's default
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \  # full access
    --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
        apt-get update && apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
        echo "GPU ready!" > /var/log/startup.log'
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Target zone (must support the requested GPU type) |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU; `count=1` gives one GPU |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--maintenance-policy` | How the instance behaves during maintenance events |
| `--scopes` | IAM scopes granted to the instance |
| `--metadata` | Optional startup script (e.g., installing CUDA drivers) |

> 👉 **Tip:** If you’re unsure whether a zone supports a specific GPU type, run:
> ```bash
> gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="name:nvidia-tesla-a6000" --format="table(name,zone)"
> ```

---

## 2️⃣  REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s the minimal JSON payload you’d POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances
Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` and `<ZONE>` with your values, and supply a valid OAuth 2.0 bearer token (`<ACCESS_TOKEN>`).

### Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
      /* <-- replace with nvidia-tesla-a6000 if available */
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y cuda-drivers\n"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]   // optional firewall tags
  }
}
```

#### Notes on the JSON fields

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `name` | Instance name (max 63 chars, lowercase letters, digits, hyphens) |
| `machineType` | Full resource path to the machine type |
| `disks[0].initializeParams.sourceImage` | Uses the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Connects to the default VPC with external IP |
| `serviceAccounts[0].scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform scope |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | Attaches one GPU of the specified type |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Startup script that runs after boot (installs CUDA drivers) |
| `tags.items` | Optional firewall tags (e.g., allow HTTP/HTTPS) |

> 📌 **Authentication** – You’ll need a valid OAuth 2.0 token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute` scope. You can obtain one via the `gcloud auth print-access-token` command or through a service account key.

---

## Quick Checklist Before Running

1. **Check GPU availability** in your target zone:
   ```bash
   gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="name:nvidia-tesla-a6000" --format="table(name,zone)"
   ```
2. **Ensure the zone supports the selected machine type** (`n1-standard-8` is widely available).
3. **Verify you have enough quota** for GPUs in that zone (`nvidia-tesla-a100` or `nvidia-tesla-a6000`).
4. **Confirm billing is enabled** for your project.

Once you’ve verified those points, either run the `gcloud` command above or POST the JSON payload to the REST endpoint. Your instance should come up with an NVIDIA GPU attached and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS ready to use. Happy computing!
